evals.prompt: Here is my transcript (BSc Applied Mathematics, Hanoi). I have the APS interview in three weeks. Make me a revision book of my courses so I can explain them to the panel.
evals.expected_output: Exam mode. One intake batch, then a Part plan table (subjects grouping courses, weak grades marked, each Part's style (Foundation cases-first, Depth map-first) and recurring pattern, thesis Part, then Gaps and Strategy) awaiting confirmation. Weak subjects are cases-first, familiar ones map-first; the recurring patterns table sits in Strategy. Parts built only from course names are flagged as unverified scope; APS format and language are looked up live or marked link needed, never asserted.

evals.prompt: I want to really understand optimal transport. Write me study notes from these three papers, I know measure theory and convex optimisation already.
evals.expected_output: Topic mode. Parts are subtopics grounded in the three papers; connections link to measure theory and convex duality; the central idea of each Part uses two close worked cases with a Compare-before-reading-on prompt before the alignment table, and each Part is cases-first, with the alignment table on a page after the compare box, and ends with a no-hint transfer question whose hint and You-have-it-if check each have their own page; recurring patterns, if any, are collected in a closing table; the Overview gives how to read, why the book is built this way, checkable outcomes and a learning map before any content Part, without stating a principle; closing questions use the Self-test title; no Gaps or Strategy Parts; ends by offering concept-exercise-generator.

evals.prompt: Make me a deep-dive book on how vLLM's PagedAttention works, version 0.6. I'll be modifying the scheduler.
evals.expected_output: Deep-dive mode. Version recorded on the title page; each interface or behaviour claim cites the paper, docs, or a source file at that version, or is marked unverified; depth goes to the scheduler; the Overview shows the system map without giving away how components work; worked examples are small numerical traces, not code listings.
Should NOT trigger study-book: a live explanation in chat belongs to professor-mentor-technical-teaching.

evals.prompt: Give me practice problems from easy to hard on Markov chains with solutions.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger study-book: a graded exercise set belongs to concept-exercise-generator.

evals.prompt: I'm new to derivatives. I know functions, rates and limits. Write me a study book Part on the derivative.
evals.expected_output: Topic mode, cases-first. In the printed order: title, a Before-you-start line, the question, two close worked cases, Compare before reading on, alignment table, then the principle. Nothing before the compare box (headings, Overview, captions) states the principle; the map appears at the end under Putting it together; the transfer question names no concept; the alignment table starts on a page after the compare box; the hint and a You-have-it-if check each have their own page; no recurring pattern is invented for a single Part. Where the reader can already predict a result, a Predict-before-reading-on box names the decision before the answer, the answer says what a plausible wrong guess should send them back to, no generic think-first prompt appears, and no closing question repeats a worked example. Evidence that overturns a plausible verdict appears after its prediction box, and no summary, hint or answer claims more than the worked material.

evals.prompt: Revision book for my oral exam: Linear Algebra (grade A, I know it well) and Measure Theory (grade C, shaky). Lecture notes attached.
evals.expected_output: Exam mode. The plan marks Linear Algebra map-first and Measure Theory cases-first. A pattern is listed only if it appears in both with nameable correspondences; if so the reusing Part has a Seen-before box after its principle and Strategy holds the patterns table.

evals.prompt: Study book on optimisation from the attached notes. Make it Depth by default; I know convex analysis well, but stochastic methods are new to me.
evals.expected_output: Topic mode. The plan table shows a style per Part: Depth everywhere by the stated default, except the stochastic-methods Parts, which their signal makes Foundation. Foundation Parts are cases-first with figures for shape, quantity, process and structure sections and no filler; Depth Parts are map-first with proofs, why each assumption is needed, and counterexamples; every content Part ends with a transfer question with no figure that gives away the method (none, or one in a deliberately different form).
